C3 failed in rollout 3 likely due to the same visit_times encoding mismatch. C4 failed in rollout 2 where medication_time was encoded as "7:00 PM (19:00)" with parenthetical notation, suggesting a formatting threshold issue.

fix_instructions: The primary failure mode is ENCODING MISMATCH driven by a structural contradiction between C6 and C7. (1) C6 expects visit_times to contain 19:30 (from PF1), but PF2's medication_time of 19:00 logically requires overriding the evening visit to 19:00 — the model correctly does this in commitments but C6 checks the decisions.visit_times field. Fix C6 by either: (a) changing it to verify that the morning visit is 07:30 and that the evening visit is either 19:30 or adjusted to 19:00 to accommodate PF2, or (b) splitting C6 into two checks: one for the morning visit time (07:30, gated by PF1) and one verifying the evening visit was adjusted from 19:30 to 19:00 when PF2 is present. (2) C7 should verify that the medication_administration commitment exists and specifies 19:00, 2 tablespoons wet food, and not crushed — if it additionally checks visit_times alignment, relax it to accept either decisions.visit_times or the visit_schedule commitment detail as evidence. (3) For C3 (failed in rollout 3): verify whether C3 checks visit_times containing 19:30 — if so, apply the same fix as C6. (4) For C4 (failed in rollout 2): the medication_time was encoded as "7:00 PM (19:00)" — if C4 uses an exact string match, update it to accept formats including parenthetical 24-hour notation, or normalize the field before comparison. (5) Ensure all time-related checks accept both 12-hour ("7:00 PM", "7:30 AM") and 24-hour ("19:00", "07:30") encodings, since rollouts use mixed formats.
